_why_two_claims: AGREEMENT asks whether the engines compute the same thing; RECOVERY asks whether they compute the right thing. Neither implies the other.

truth.source: the fixture's true curve, itself a restricted cubic spline with the same knots, so there is no approximation error

agreement.claim: both engines report the same predictions and contrast, from two different spline bases
agreement._note: Observed spread on the committed fixture: 0 at ten significant digits on every key, although R fits ns()'s B-spline basis and Python Harrell's truncated-power basis: the same function space, so the same curve. harness/flexible_examples.test.py checks against a third, rescaled basis and shows quantile-placed knots give a contrast of 21.53 against 22.64.

recovery.claim: the predictions and contrast are close to the true curve's

calibration.rule: about 1.3 times the measured 99th percentile miss, rounded up
calibration.limits: Measured by harness/flexible_examples.test.py over seeds 0 to 99 of this generator.
